lead.headline: Taylor flops and hits the trade market; Bloodsports lead by 48
lead.deck: 1-6, heading to 2-6. 124.5 to 76.2 with Daniels tonight and Loveland Monday.
lead.body: The bad news is Jonathan Taylor: 6.7 points on eight carries in a 42-7 loss at Jacksonville — no injury, a blowout — and the Colts, who moved Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, are now fielding calls on him before the 10 November deadline, with the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers checking in. A trade could raise or cut his role; nothing to do until it happens. Josh Jacobs stays eligible for Week 9, though Rapoport says a suspension is possible once the league finishes reviewing new allegations. Everything else carried the week: Tuten 29.9, Jacobs 23.2, Golden 20.9, the Jaguars D/ST 19.5. Daniels is good to go tonight with no designation and Loveland plays Monday. No claim is worth never-resetting priority.

doFirst.deck: Daniels and Loveland are set; no claim is worth priority.
doFirst.note: No claims — priority never resets, and nothing on the wire is a starter here.
doFirst.empty: Nothing left to decide this week: Daniels plays tonight and Loveland Monday, both cleared.

roster.deck: The lineup as set is the projection lineup (126.4); Daniels and Loveland are the only starters left, neither in doubt.

wire.deck: Allgeier and Mike Washington Jr. are the afternoon's risers; neither is a starter here and IPADE priority never resets.
